clauses.current_legal_basis: The provision continues because no end is stated and no instrument ending EO 12465 was found in the searches checked through 2026-10-14: Section 1 designation of the lead agency.
clauses.reason: Section 1 designates the Department of Transportation as the lead agency within the Federal government for encouraging and facilitating commercial expendable launch vehicle (ELV) activities by the United States private sector. It states no end, no held later instrument amends it, and the searches show no revocation of the order, so it is operative on 2026-10-14. The Federal regulation 49 CFR 1.83(f), found by the eCFR search, still assigns the Secretary the functions under this order; that is a lead and is not relied on as the legal basis.

clauses.current_legal_basis: The provision continues because no end is stated and no instrument ending EO 12465 was found in the searches checked through 2026-10-14: Section 2 functions of the lead agency.
clauses.reason: Section 2 directs the Secretary of Transportation, to the extent permitted by law and subject to appropriations, to act as a focal point for private sector launch contacts, promote commercial ELV operations, lead streamlining of licensing procedures, consult on consistent licensing, serve as single point of contact for licensing documentation, recommend administrative streamlining, identify adverse statutes and regulations, and plan for long-term effects (paragraphs (a) to (h)). It states no end, no held later instrument amends it, and the searches show no revocation of the order, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

clauses.current_legal_basis: The provision continues because no end is stated and no instrument ending EO 12465 was found in the searches checked through 2026-10-14: Section 3 interagency group.
clauses.reason: Section 3 establishes an interagency group, chaired by the Secretary of Transportation and composed of representatives of the Departments of State, Defense and Commerce, the Federal Communications Commission and the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, to meet at the call of the Chair and advise and assist the Department of Transportation. It sets no term or sunset, and no held instrument abolishes the group or revokes the order, so the establishment remains in force on 2026-10-14; whether the group still meets is not a legal ending and no source was found showing it was abolished.

clauses.current_legal_basis: The provision continues because no end is stated and no instrument ending EO 12465 was found in the searches checked through 2026-10-14: Section 4 responsibilities of other agencies.
clauses.reason: Section 4 directs all executive departments and agencies to assist the Secretary of Transportation and, to the extent permitted by law and in consultation with the Secretary, to provide information on regulatory actions, review and revise regulations to remove unnecessary obstacles, and set timetables for handling ELV licence applications (paragraphs (a) to (c)). It states no end, no held later instrument amends it, and the searches show no revocation of the order, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

clauses.current_legal_basis: The provision continues because no end is stated and no instrument ending EO 12465 was found in the searches checked through 2026-10-14: Section 5 non-diminution of other authority.
clauses.reason: Section 5 provides that the Secretary's powers under the order shall not diminish or abrogate any statutory or operational authority of any other Federal agency. It states no end, no held later instrument amends it, and the searches show no revocation of the order, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

clauses.current_legal_basis: The provision continues because no end is stated and no instrument ending EO 12465 was found in the searches checked through 2026-10-14: Section 6 no private rights.
clauses.reason: Section 6 provides that nothing in the order or in procedures promulgated under it confers a substantive or procedural right enforceable against the United States, its agencies, officers or any person. It states no end, no held later instrument amends it, and the searches show no revocation of the order, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

clauses.current_legal_basis: The provision continues because no end is stated and no instrument ending EO 12465 was found in the searches checked through 2026-10-14: Section 7 effective date.
clauses.reason: Section 7 provides that the order is effective immediately. The order took effect on issuance, February 24, 1984, and the clause states no end; with the order unrevoked it remains operative on 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
Read the held Federal Register text of EO 12465 (49 FR 7211, February 28, 1984; jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12465.txt) in full. It designates the Department of Transportation as lead agency for commercial expendable launch vehicle activities (Section 1), lists the Secretary's functions (Section 2), establishes an interagency group (Section 3), directs other agencies to assist (Section 4), preserves other agencies' authority (Section 5), creates no private rights (Section 6) and takes effect immediately (Section 7). The prepared inventory cuts Section 4 at the Federal Register page break and omits the text on the next page, so the inventory is corrected to seven clauses by characters. The order states no duration or condition. The three bounded machine searches were read (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes with zero hits); the hits in the U.S. Code and eCFR are leads only (the order is printed as a note to 51 U.S.C. 50903 and 49 CFR 1.83(f) assigns the Secretary the functions under it) and are not relied on as a legal basis. The held-corpus number search finds only the order, its 1989 codification SOURCE line and later regulations citing it. Every clause is therefore operative on 2026-10-14 under the held original plus bounded search route. Limits: the U.S. Code search does not reflect laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14; the text is the OCR layer of the official page, which includes an editorial note that misprints the order number.
